experiment.name: Admission phenotype associations, BET cohort (article 1)
experiment.description: Every pair of admission variables tested with a type-appropriate rank or contingency test, permutation p values, Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across the run. Exploratory: associations, not causes, and no severity label exists in this dataset.
experiment.summary: 740 pairs tested among 39 variables in 150 subjects (28 numeric/ordinal, 11 categorical). 172 pairs have BH-adjusted p < 0.05, of which 12 are arithmetic (trivial) and 160 are findings to look at. 6 variable clusters at |rho| >= 0.4.

results.title: Spearman correlation matrix (numeric and ordinal variables)

sections.heading: What was tested
paragraphs: 150 subjects from dataset DS05 (Prevalence of Ehrlichia canis or Theileria equi co-infections in dogs that are naturally infected and clinically sick due to babesiosis). 39 variables were tested in every pairing: 28 numeric or ordinal and 11 categorical, grouped by domain as signalment: Age, Body weight, Sex, Breed group; clinical: Duration of illness, Rectal temperature, Pulse rate, Respiratory rate, Peripheral lymph node enlargement, Habitus (mental status) score, Ticks present, Panting at examination, Pale mucous membranes, Icteric mucous membranes, Primary complaint includes IA, Primary complaint includes L, Primary complaint includes HGUR, Primary complaint includes WL; haematology: Haemoglobin, Red cell count, Haematocrit, Mean cell volume, Mean cell haemoglobin, Mean cell haemoglobin concentration, Red cell distribution width, White cell count, Segmented neutrophils, Band neutrophils, Lymphocytes, Monocytes, Eosinophils, Platelet count, Nucleated red cells, Reticulocytes, Absolute reticulocyte count; biochemistry: Total serum protein, Albumin, Globulin; time: Season.

Each pair got a test that fits its types: Spearman rank correlation for two numeric variables, a Kruskal-Wallis or Mann-Whitney test with an eta-squared effect size for a category against a number, and a chi-square test with Cramer's V for two categories. P values come from 5,000 permutations rather than a distributional formula, and all 740 tests were adjusted together with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at a false discovery rate of 0.05. The smallest p value a permutation test can report is about 1 in 5,000, so the strongest associations share one floor value and are not ranked among themselves by p.

The heatmap shows the Spearman correlation between every pair of numeric variables: warm cells are positive, cool cells negative, and the neutral mid-tone is no correlation. Pairs where one variable is an arithmetic function of the other (for example a calculated index and the measurements it is calculated from) are marked trivial and excluded from the findings below, because they must correlate.

sections.heading: How the parameters group
paragraphs: Average-linkage clustering on 1 minus the absolute correlation, cut at |rho| of 0.4, groups the numeric variables into 6 blocks that move together. Read these as descriptive groupings of measurements, not as patient subtypes.
Total serum protein and Globulin (mean |rho| 0.80). Part of this block is arithmetic: some members are calculated from others.
Haemoglobin, Haematocrit, Red cell count and Habitus (mental status) score (mean |rho| 0.76).
Mean cell volume and Mean cell haemoglobin (mean |rho| 0.63).
White cell count, Segmented neutrophils, Band neutrophils, Monocytes and Lymphocytes (mean |rho| 0.58). Part of this block is arithmetic: some members are calculated from others.

Mean cell haemoglobin concentration, Red cell distribution width, Reticulocytes, Absolute reticulocyte count and Nucleated red cells (mean |rho| 0.54). Part of this block is arithmetic: some members are calculated from others.
Age and Body weight (mean |rho| 0.41).
Not in any block at this cut: Duration of illness, Rectal temperature, Pulse rate, Respiratory rate, Peripheral lymph node enlargement, Eosinophils, Platelet count, Albumin.

sections.heading: Strongest associations across domains
paragraphs: 160 non-trivial pairs stay significant after adjustment: 75 link different domains and 85 sit within one domain. The cross-domain pairs are the ones most likely to say something new, because within-domain correlations among laboratory values are largely expected.
Haematocrit rises with Habitus (mental status) score (Spearman rho +0.54) (n = 145, adjusted p = 0.002).
Red cell count rises with Habitus (mental status) score (Spearman rho +0.53) (n = 145, adjusted p = 0.002).
Haemoglobin rises with Habitus (mental status) score (Spearman rho +0.52) (n = 145, adjusted p = 0.002).
Haemoglobin rises with Albumin (Spearman rho +0.45) (n = 144, adjusted p = 0.002).
Red cell count rises with Albumin (Spearman rho +0.44) (n = 144, adjusted p = 0.002).
Haematocrit rises with Albumin (Spearman rho +0.44) (n = 144, adjusted p = 0.002).
Monocytes falls as Habitus (mental status) score rises (Spearman rho -0.42) (n = 145, adjusted p = 0.002).
Rectal temperature falls as White cell count rises (Spearman rho -0.42) (n = 143, adjusted p = 0.002).
Rectal temperature rises with Haematocrit (Spearman rho +0.41) (n = 143, adjusted p = 0.002).
Body weight rises with Mean cell haemoglobin (Spearman rho +0.39) (n = 148, adjusted p = 0.002).
Rectal temperature rises with Haemoglobin (Spearman rho +0.39) (n = 143, adjusted p = 0.002).
Rectal temperature rises with Red cell count (Spearman rho +0.38) (n = 143, adjusted p = 0.002).
Band neutrophils falls as Habitus (mental status) score rises (Spearman rho -0.37) (n = 145, adjusted p = 0.002).
Age rises with Globulin (Spearman rho +0.36) (n = 144, adjusted p = 0.002).
A further 61 cross-domain pairs are in the findings table, ordered by adjusted p and effect size.

sections.heading: Signalment, season and other host factors
paragraphs: Age: 5 associations survive adjustment, with Body weight, Globulin, Total serum protein, Respiratory rate, Pulse rate. The strongest is: Age rises with Body weight (Spearman rho +0.41) (n = 150, adjusted p = 0.002).

Body weight: 12 associations survive adjustment, with Age, Mean cell haemoglobin, Mean cell haemoglobin concentration, Pulse rate, Breed group, Rectal temperature, Total serum protein, Haemoglobin and 4 more. The strongest is: Age rises with Body weight (Spearman rho +0.41) (n = 150, adjusted p = 0.002).
Season: no association survived adjustment. With 150 subjects this excludes large effects, not small ones.
Sex: no association survived adjustment. With 150 subjects this excludes large effects, not small ones.

Breed group: 4 associations survive adjustment, with Body weight, Mean cell haemoglobin, Habitus (mental status) score, Absolute reticulocyte count. The strongest is: Body weight differs by breed group and is highest where breed group is Boerboel (medians Boerboel: 34.8, Crossbreed: 17.15, Other purebred: 23.85, Pitbull: 17; eta squared 0.17) (n = 150, adjusted p = 0.002).

sections.heading: Variables with no surviving association
paragraphs: Peripheral lymph node enlargement, Eosinophils, Ticks present, Panting at examination, Primary complaint includes IA, Primary complaint includes WL. Each of these was tested against every other variable and nothing passed the false discovery threshold. That is informative in itself when the variable was expected to track others, and unremarkable for rare or near-constant variables.

sections.heading: How far to trust this
paragraphs: Associations, not causes: every value was taken at one admission, so the direction of any relationship is not identifiable from these data.

150 subjects against 39 variables is a small sample for 740 tests. The false discovery rate controls the expected share of false positives among the reported findings, not the chance that any one finding is real, and effect sizes near the threshold should be treated as leads.
The dataset carries no outcome or severity label, so no finding here can be read as prognostic. Any severity reading relies on clinical proxies such as habitus or anaemia grade.
Categorical levels with fewer than 8 subjects were merged into Other or dropped, so rare breeds, complaints or groups are not tested on their own.
Variable clusters are a summary of the correlation matrix. They describe which measurements co-vary and should not be called phenotypes or subtypes without an independent cohort.
